evidence: The paper uses 8 epistasis-detection tools (GBOOST, PLINK, FastEpistasis, etc.) to identify SNP-SNP interactions, not variable importance scoring. It does not rank or interpret importance magnitudes. Conclusions rest on enrichment tests against drug databases (hypergeometric/permutation tests) and empirical validation: 5 of 9 predicted drug combinations showed synergistic effects in MCF-7 cell assays, and filtering with 3D genome data improved clinical hit rates from 6.6% to 20.4%. Though Ranger is evaluated as one epistasis method, the paper notes it "failed to identify any significantly associated SNP pairs" and does not use its importance outputs.
